root_cause: A refactor moved the noise-offset application from the dequantized float scalefactor (sce->sf, which was numerically safe to add an offset to) onto the raw integer scalefactor-offset value (sce->sfo) that is later used directly as an array index/lookup-table offset, without adding any bounds clamp on the new value. The bitstream-controlled noise.offset field combined with repeated/attacker-influenced sfo values allowed the stored offset to become large enough to index outside the pow2sf lookup table.
findings: In apply_noise_fill(), when a scalefactor band is fully quantized to zero and noise filling is applied, the code adds noise_offset (derived from ue->noise.offset - 16, an 8-bit field that ranges roughly -16..15) directly onto sce->sfo[g*ics->max_sfb + sfb] with no lower-bound clamp: `sce->sfo[g*ics->max_sfb + sfb] += noise_offset;`.
